39.14: And they perish, their souls, and the soul of all the people; for God commanded men that they should hear the commandment of the priests, if they command them in that which is commanded.
39.15: And when they transgress them, they take destruction forever.
39.16: As the hosts of the Devil: and when men heard the commandment of the Devil for their head, and obeyed him in that which God breaks, and were kept back from the praises and the holiness, and went out with him, forever.
39.17: Likewise shall fall and perish everyone who goes out from the house of the Christians, by wrath the priests shall drive him out, before the offering is fulfilled.
39.18: And if they hear concerning them, in that which God does not promise, they take judgment with them, as the hosts of the Devil were judged with him; likewise he who holds back at the time of the Holy One, and does not hear the declaration of the books and of the holiness, and is adorned, takes judgment upon me; for he is, instead of him who runs for Christ, they polish him; for he is he who takes by an unclean spirit and an unclean body.
39.19: And you are he: as the books and the holiness made them hosts before the offering, they sanctify the faithful, and His ascension they cleanse, as I have shown you; and after this it is fitting to take the offering, as men cannot be, who are without sin, for one hour that abides in the wilderness alone.
39.20: And he who shall be joined with men, causing to sin, burns from her by a word which is not fitting; or by an oath, or by reviling, or by a curse of his neighbor.
39.21: Or by withholding from this: he is he who in these works abode, and was defiled, and was cleansed; and he wishes for the hearing of the reading of the books, and the hearing of the prayer of light, that he may cast away his defilement, and be sanctified.
39.22: And after this he eats and drinks from the holy flesh and the blood of Christ; and he is holy, and is converted; and he who does not love the books and the holiness, and is confounded, shall be reckoned — his body shall be reckoned, and his blood is for Christ; and he also is unclean.
39.23: And Christ shall humble him again exceedingly; He said in the tongue of the prophet: "Be humbled"; for He said in the tongue of the prophet: "Be humbled; for him who humbles me I will exalt, and I will honor him who honored me"; and He swore this, as the likeness of him who sows seed in earth which is not watered, and does not plow it; he also destroys the seed, and it does not sprout for the earth.
39.24: Likewise men, if he was in fatherhood, sought you, as you sow for you: he shall be as earth, a thing of many defilements; and if he comes into the house of Kerkemtedan, and hears the voice of their books, and the Gospel, the voice of God — the water of life — as the LORD God said; and he is watered by that water from newness, that cleanses sin.
39.25: And when he is watered, and Tesfa comes, the Holy Spirit descends upon him, and cleanses him from sin, as earth is cleansed from defilement.
39.26: And then he receives the holy offering, and bears fruit in him, as earth that is opened, the chosen one, that bears the seed that is sown, and it bears fruit in it.
39.27: Behold, I have shown you the glory and the holiness which is equal upon all the faithful; and apart from Him they cannot do anything at all from the commandment of God; for by the glory the Holy Spirit abides in them, and the unclean spirits are driven out from them, and they are made to do the work for God.
39.28: And whoever departs from going to the house of the Christians in the morning and in the evening, and departs from their prayer at the time of the Holy One, as I have told you, and reaches death in that day, and shall be reckoned forever and ever — as the Devil and his hosts fell from her — and behold, I have shown you the glory and the holiness, that it is fitting upon all the faithful, all of them, at all the days of their life.
39.29: For God has appointed for them these works — they are the cause of their salvation and of what is their life; and this is it: that in every day and in every night, seven and two hours, God appointed for them three times to reach to the gate of the house of the Christians, in the morning, and in the evening, and at the time of the Holy One; and these three times at which the Christian reaches to the gate are not the measure of two hours; and there remains for them seven and two hours, in which they do the work of the flesh that passes away; and God gives them from the wealth of this world a doubled reward, in place of the work which they forsook, in place of those two hours, while it is charged to them upon that which cleanses them, for the life of their souls — which is His glory, of God, and His holiness, and the descent of the Holy Spirit upon them, and the forgiveness of their sins.
39.30: And likewise in every week, seven days, God has appointed upon men their work, that it rule not over him.
39.31: And He said to them: "Work the work of the flesh two days, and work for the spirit one day."
39.32: And in that one day, work in it the work that is spiritual, from morning until evening; it shall be for you in it a work without reading the word of God in the holy house of the Christians. And He said again: "When you read, a good reading read." And all who are gathered to you, and you do for them, God shall give you a reward on their account, in the kingdom.

40.1: And if you do not know, you shall not do; do not go to another city, until you shall see that which abides for you; as you go, you seek the work of this world in the district which has no sacrifice, to the other which has a sacrifice.
40.2: And the day of the life of the Spirit passes from you without work; because you do not know, that you — until the other day — shall not, that you may find the life of your spirit; truly God commanded that He not do the work of this world on the day of rest; therefore that men should forsake everything, and abide in the holy books, which are the spiritual life, and should pray over it without delay, and be occupied in labors, as he does the border of eternal life; for the reading of the books of God cleanses the soul and the body, and they are cleansed from sin, in the portion for His disciples, in the holy Gospel; truly it is a vineyard, and its fathers withered, and every ordinance that bears no fruit and dies is done; and that which bears fruit is it that is cleansed, as He created many, and it was fulfilled.
40.3: Behold, I have shown you in this word which I have told you in it.
40.4: It is shown: they shall spring up; men shall be cleansed from all of it, and shall bear fruit, the fruit of eternal life.
40.5: And he who does not hear the word, and does not speak His books continually, shall be without fruit; and his Father cuts him off from the burden of the Son, as they cut off the branch from the vineyard.
40.6: And he who speaks the books continually on the holy day, he abides in Christ, as the branch abides in the vineyard; for the cleansing of Christ cleanses him, and sanctifies him from his sin, and causes him to bear — he bears — the fruit of eternal life.
40.7: Beloved, this — and for the rest which we have mentioned, the hours of the faithful; and in them they shall overcome the satans — which is our going to the house of the Christians in the morning and in the evening, at every time; and we tarry at the time of the Holy One without ceasing, from the, until it is fulfilled.
40.8: And the hearing of the books of God on the holy day — all of it, and to the rest; if men work continually, He abides, in it the Holy Spirit; and he shall be continually who is born of God; and there shall not be over him the hosts of sin.
40.9: As John the evangelist said in the epistle: "For everyone who is born of God does not sin; for his seed abides firm, and he cannot sin; for he is born of God."
40.10: And again he said in it: "He who is born of God keeps himself, and the evil one does not draw near to touch him."
40.11: And all the faithful who are baptized — they are born of God — as the seed of the Holy Spirit abides firm in them, by which they are born of God; and He keeps them from the evil one and from the hosts; and they cannot sin; but they do good, without their desire; for the Holy Spirit works for them over him; for He is firm in them; and He loves to abide in them; if he keeps these commandments, He abides in them, and keeps them from the evil one; and they have no power to sin, for the Holy Spirit hinders them from sin, and keeps them from the evil one who draws them into the doing of sin.
40.12: And if they sin by weakness, then the Holy Spirit who dwells in them takes them, and draws them to shame by leave; and likewise if they forsake one of these three commandments, the Holy Spirit forsakes them, and an unclean, evil spirit overcomes them, and draws them to the doing of sin, by work and by violence; and God shall not be in them, if it be so; knowledge: he who is born of God does not sin.
40.13: As John the apostle said: Behold, what is the greatness from these commandments, by which it shall be that men delight with Christ, the Son of God, in the glory of the kingdom; and he shall be who is born of God.
40.14: And they are not fat, and are not drunk, and have no weariness; and sweat does not perish as and thirst; and sweat does not perish; for he is he who from of old goes to the work of this world; he goes forth to the house of the Christians; and after its fulfillment, work — he goes to her in the evening; and sweat does not perish.
40.15: And at the time of the Holy One, if all — all — at every time, its measure is as one hour.
40.16: From seven and seven hours — and there is not in this again a — in those festivals they shall find the seeking of eternal life in the kingdom of heaven; and God gives a doubled [reward] instead of that which they have left in those two other days, concerning the trading of the holy day; for fatness is grace; it is in His fatness.
40.17: As He said in the tongue of the prophet: "I who slew, and I make alive; I am He who burns; I who smote, and I heal; whom I heal."
40.18: But He gives to men a double [reward] instead of that which they have left from the work of this world, as He said in the holy Gospel — He said: "Do not be anxious for what you shall eat, and for what you shall drink; for the nations seek all this; and your Father who is in heaven knows that you are in need of all this, of which you are needy;" but this [seek you] first: the kingdom and the righteousness; and it shall be given to you a double [reward] instead of that which was left from us, for the sake of this seeking, that took the kingdom and the righteousness; and it shall be given to us a double [reward] instead of that which is without the reading of the word of God, first; for He is the Father of us all, and He is He who gives us that which is fitting, and that which is fitting, and that which is fitting; for He knows that we desire — we seek all this; He gives to us the kingdom; and He reckons to us all this; He is He who gives to us; for He is He who, as we are humbled, strengthens us for this temporal world. Behold, beloved: these three commandments, keep them; for they are the salvation of everyone who believes in Christ; and in them they overcome the evil enemy, who is he who prevails over them; and they have no power over him, without these three commandments.
40.19: For in them the Holy Spirit abides firm in them, and strengthens them against the evil host, and they overcome him, while they are upon the earth in the flesh.
40.20: And after their going forth from the flesh, He gives them victory over the hosts of the Devil in the air, and saves them — joy and life forever.
40.21: And the evil one, moreover — when he knew that these three commandments are they, a fence for the faithful, and in them they overcome him — and he proceeds against them in their, and hinders the enemy, and troubles them from them, until he separate them from her, and the Holy Spirit forsakes them, and he prevails over them, and destroys them.
40.22: And they, moreover, beloved, shall burn in faith; readiness shall be with them, as a wall, that they may receive in it the buckler, the darts of Satan and his spears shall trouble them from them — the commandments.
40.23: As the apostle Paul said in the epistle to the people of Ephesus: "Take the sword of the Holy Spirit, which is the word of God, in all those [times], and in all, while you pray at every time in the Holy Spirit; and be watchful over this, at every time."
40.24: I show that the word of God, which abides in it — or which abides upon him — and His glory and His holiness continually, is the sword of the Holy Spirit, which is in truth.

41.1: For men — if he keeps the three commandments — but they are fat; and the giving of the Mass and the work shall be, by the Holy Spirit, firm in him; and he is the sword of God: when the hosts of Satan see him, they flee from him, and cannot draw near to him; and they resist, and they accuse men, those who transgress one of these three commandments and forsake it; the Holy Spirit is resisted over him; as with a man who has in his hand a sharp sword, polished: his enemies cannot draw near to him, from fear of the sword; and they stand from afar, and they cast at him with stones and sling-stones; and the sword falls from his hand; and they cry out to him; and he also desires that there be in his hand a shield, with the sword; and when they cast at him with stones, he receives them in it, and it falls from his hand.
41.2: And your shield is faith, by which a man can keep these three commandments; the satans shall not draw near to it, who trouble them from her.
41.3: As Paul says in his epistle to the men of Ephesus:
41.4: "Seek the shield of faith, which is the sword of the Holy Spirit, by which the quenching of all his arrows of the evil one, which are full of fire, is possible."
41.5: It is shown that men cannot be joined to the glory and the holiness and the speaking of the word of God — which is the sword of the Holy Spirit — if there be not with him the shield of faith, by which he destroys the arrows of the evil one.
41.6: And I also show you the arrows, that by them he overcomes, if he believes, if he keeps the three commandments. The first arrow: when a man who believes goes to the house of the Christians for the glory and for the Mass and for the speaking of the word of God, Satan aims at him the work of this world, and stops [it] in his breath, that he is he who, if he went to the house of the Christians and tarried for the passing, shall pass from him the likeness, thus and thus, and causes him to lose the profit.
41.7: And when he hears from Satan this counsel, and transgresses that which is fitting for him, the sword falls from his hand, which is the Holy Spirit; and if it be that his possession is the shield of faith, it is not bent for Satan, a portion for that which he adorned for him from the work of this world, and that which he strengthened in his handful from the lost profit of the likeness — those who give him say: Christ, your fathers, righteousness is departed from you; he says: "I will not forsake my likeness to pass away, and I will not let my work perish, that which passed me." For he is he who says: "Seek first my kingdom and my righteousness, and all this shall be added to you." And if he believes thus, he overcomes the thought of Satan by the shield of faith; and he is joined to the glory and to the Mass and the reading, firm — the sword in his hand — and overcomes by it his enemy; and he shall be a counsel that is greater than the counsels of the martyrs, who endured their strife with the flesh, or in their likeness. And his strife, this one, is with the hosts of Satan, spirits of fire, who have dominion over all the earth, as Paul says; and his counsel, at that time, is greater than the counsels of the martyrs; for he stood firm and burned with the helps of the satans, and the roughness of those who burned the martyrs.
41.8: Behold, I have shown you the first arrow; and this is the second arrow: If a man wishes to be joined in the speaking on the holy day, and goes to the house of the Christians for the glory and for the Mass, every time, and fears Satan, and speaks: Let us not find in the way, one draws near to you thus and thus, lest he delay you, or crush you, or kill you; and if he listened from him, and despises that which is fitting for him, he forsakes the Holy Spirit, who is the sword, and Satan his enemy resists over him, and destroys him. If there was with him the shield of faith, he gives him and says to him: "The lying Satan cannot at all delay me, and crush me, and torment me, and kill me, without the will of Christ, my strength; and if He willed it, He would do it by me."
41.9: And when you hid yourself in a cave of the earth, he does not come to you, and my does not rise to work by you; he cannot at all work evil by you. And when it was thus, I was lifted up above the beasts; for the hairs of my head are numbered.
41.10: And he is in this [way]; and he is he who says thus: "For two sparrows are sold for two farthings; and one of them does not fall, says He, to the earth, without the will of your Father who is in heaven."
41.11: And to you also, all the hairs of your head are numbered; and he is, by this shield of faith, he who overcomes his enemy, and is resisted over him; and the sword abides in his hand, which is the Holy Spirit; and there shall be a reward in this.
41.12: The second is greater than the first.
41.13: For he is he who gave over his head to Christ, exceedingly, more than the martyrs; and he endured the tree of His cross, and followed Him, and believed; for they who kill him and destroy him are those who are without Him; and behold, I have shown you the second arrow. The arrow of the veil: and when it was for a man — from a work that is done by it, from the keeping of these three commandments, and the fear which they fear for him by it, for Satan, until they are cut off from the veil.
41.14: And Satan comes upon him secretly, and presses upon him, until the sword falls from his hand, and he resists over him; and the sin of this boaster, from sinners, is a sin; for he is he who was exalted, and was lifted up from the speaking and the glory and the Mass, without a cause.

42.1: And if his pretext became the purity of the faith — it is this which drives Satan, weakened, away from him; and he says to his soul: "You had power, O Satan, to cast me down — and not by deed."
42.2: He wishes now that he may cast me down in weakness and in destruction — the destruction in which he himself fell from heaven; for Satan and his hosts, when they were shut out from the glory of God and from His holiness, and were troubled and troubled exceedingly — or else they desired sin — [were cast down] from the kingdom of heaven; and He created me, that I might inherit their kingdom, from which they fell; and if you trouble me [to depart] from His glory and His holiness, and from the reading of the books of God, and trouble me even as they [were troubled], I fall from Him, even as they fell.
42.3: And by this thought of good — which is the purity of the faith — he overcomes them, and does that which is fitting for him [to do] before the glory of God and His holiness and the reading of His books; and he is joined in fellowship with His martyrs who were slain; and he overcame, and took the crown of victory, and the kingdom of heaven abides with Christ in the kingdom which endures forever.
42.4: And know, friend, that by these three cords Satan enters into the believer at all times and at every hour, that he may trouble them and bring them to the three commands; and he does not strive to cease from the crown of victory, nor shall the kingdom of heaven be fitting for them; and know: he who is fought against departs by one of all the cords, and overcomes, and goes to the house of the Christians, with more joy than [the joy] which is without fighting; and the believer is fitting, that he be guarded, and that he keep for the time; and he causes men to stumble by stumbling from these three cords; and from him, at one time, there comes a hearing from him, and glory at all times.
42.5: Upon him, in the assembly: from him he does not fear; and if he does not hear — from him he does not fear; and if he does not hear, that he should turn back to him: for he is not able to dwell in the fence, and he does not rebuke in it a second time; for by a sniffing he snorts; and if he snort once, and there entered a fence into it, he does not always leave from dwelling.
42.6: And concerning this the apostles commanded the believers, and ordained for them: for to you [belong] the prayers of the morning and the prayers of the evening; these are the prayers — at the second [hour], and at the third, and at the fourth hour, and at the hour of the evening meal, and in the spirit of the evening meal.
42.7: These three prayers are added upon those prayers; they are fitting for them, [to pray] wherever they will.
42.8: Until there is for them no work: they are fitting for them in unity and in deed.
42.9: And again, the priests shall not neglect one of them, that the enemy may not prevail over them and overcome them; for by this they drive them away at all times.
42.10: And as for those who are weak in the work of the flesh, these three prayers are not fitting for them — without the prayer of supplication; they are fitting for them, in their houses, with prayer and with prostration, that they may dwell in the house of the Christian in the morning and the evening; for it is a guard for them from Satan and his hosts, when they sleep; for there came in [a time] of making them to forget their entering in, and they know not until they awaken them; one comes and reproves him; and behold, Satan shows them his form [in sleep]; swiftly he casts them down [like] a demon, and by making them forget, and they do not awaken — those who are indeed sleeping; and if a man has prayed the prayer of supplication, he is not able — Satan — to appear to him, nor to cast him down.
42.11: And if at all the supplication is mingled with those [prayers] — arise; these: do not reckon upon them sin; for the prayer is reckoned to them [as] falsehood, which is not [reckoned] at the completion of his days; this is the prayer which is fitting upon all the believers; but those who are weak in the work of the flesh — no — and women, freewomen, and servants, great and small.
42.12: And these one prayers: the third, and the second, and the fifth, and the half of the night are fitting for them, while they do their work.
42.13: Then they stand — or they bow down.
42.14: Or prostrate, or in every work; for God reckons to them their prayers, as He reckons to those who have no work; these stand and spend the night, while they watch; He said: their spending the night — God reckons to them their prayer on account of their weariness in the work of the flesh, which presses upon them; and the prayer of the morning and of the evening and of supplication are fitting for them; He adds them with fear and trembling and prostration from them in the house of the Christian; the prayer of the morning and the evening, and the prayer of supplication in their houses; for they are not in the house of the Christian to pray — [it is] rather in their houses.
42.15: And as David the prophet said in the Psalm of the hundred and second: "My soul, my soul, I will sing to You."
42.16: He took away my sins from me for Your sake; and likewise He said thus: "In Your sanctuary I appeared to You, that I might behold Your newness."
42.17: And in the Psalm: "In the multitude of Your mercy I will enter Your house, and I will worship in the court of Your sanctuary."
42.18: And in the Psalm of the ninth: "Before Your angels I will sing, and I will worship in the court of Your sanctuary."
42.19: And concerning this it is fitting that the prayer of the morning and the evening be in the house of the Christian.
42.20: For these two prayers, they are the firstfruits of the day and of the night; and the prayer of supplication, let it be in the house; and these other one prayers, they pray them where a man is, in, according to the measure of their strength and by it.
42.21: For at the hour of the third hour there descended upon it the Holy Spirit upon the apostles, and they were comforted and strengthened, and He taught them all the mysteries of heaven and of earth; and it is the prayer of the Holy Spirit, and in it the believers are renewed; and in it they scourged Jesus Christ with scourgings; and at the seventh hour, in it Christ was crucified; and He says [in] that [hour]: the tree of the Cross.
42.22: And concerning this it is fitting for us, that we pray in it to Him who was crucified for our sake; and at the ninth hour He brought forth Adam from punishment and from the judgment of death; and in it Christ died, and broke the power of the Devil and his hosts — these are the rulers of death — and He turned Adam and his seed into Paradise; and concerning this it is fitting that we pray in it with thanksgiving and.
42.23: And in the middle of the night Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem; and in it the dead were quickened; and in it He comes to judge the living and the dead, as He said in the holy Gospel in the parable of the ten virgins.
42.24: And concerning this it is fitting that we pray in it with work and prayer and weeping; and as for those who have in them work: they shall become [worthy of] these one [prayers] which are fitting for them, according to the measure of their strength and of their power; and if they add to this, their joy shall be [greater]; for they are fitting, according to the measure of their strength and of their knowledge.
42.25: And if it be that in their work [they are occupied], save in the night of the Sabbath — [the night] in which those who have in them work in it — they are fitting for them likewise: the third, and the seventh, and the fifth, and the evening, upon the reading of the books; for on the day of the Sabbath Christ rose from the dead.
42.26: And concerning this He taught them, that they should glorify Him and sanctify Him in it always; and in it He comes to judge the living and the dead; and it is fitting for them that they read His books on the day of the Sabbath wholly, that they may be ready on that great day, and may rise with Him in His glory, as they were with Him in this world; and not as the believers [are] — as the pretext of God was completed, and He shall give wealth to him on the day of their resurrection.
42.27: So shall He rejoice with them, and give them wealth forever on the day of their resurrection; and as He is grieved with them, and they fast two days — Wednesday and Friday — these are sad in them; His helpers, on account of the suffering and the death and the crucifixion: so shall they be delivered from grief forever, and from hunger, and from one forever; and He shall give them joy forever with His helpers.

43.1: And behold, I have prepared for you, in another book, the cause of their grief for the apostles on one day — Wednesday and Friday; and I have prepared for you, in another book, the completion of His glory on the day of the Sabbath: how the fast of Wednesday and Friday is fitting upon all the believers — men, and women, and the young, and the small; and those who are perfected in them from their youth, this is fitting for them: for servants and for, in this week. These, friend, are not able to fast, and are not able to labor for Him who absolved them, and they are not able to do [it]; and whatever is good — if they have not kept all the three commands: for they, if they have not kept them, the power of the Holy Spirit is not with them, and they cannot do [it]; and whatever is good: for Satan strives against them — these three commands — and He taught all the believers; and know that God shall give you a joy which is greater than the joy of him who takes a gift; for he who takes a gift takes — and who does not die.
43.2: And by these commands, take them for the souls, from where they sinned, and free them from the hosts, and give them life forever; and keep, that you teach men this time, without weakness; for the enemy sought to blind their hearts from their heavenly [things] and from their inward [things]; for he knows that by them they shall overcome him, and they shall prevail over him by their inward [things] and be strengthened; and by the reading of the holy books, and His might and His holiness — of our Lord Jesus Christ: to Him belongs the glory, and the holiness, and the honor, and to His Father, and to the Holy Spirit, now and always, to the ages of ages. Amen.

44.1: A discourse of haste, concerning the denial of the day of the Sabbath and its completion:, friend — God shall enlighten the eyes of your heart by the light of His holy, He comforted, that you may perceive the mysteries of the kingdom.
44.2: That which I commanded you, that I should declare to you the completion of the day of holiness and glory: know that it is all the work of the day of the Sabbath; it is the day of God; and its name among all the children of baptism; for all of them call it Kyriake, in the tongue of the Greeks; its interpretation: the day of God, in which He rose from the dead; and concerning this we were commanded, that we should rejoice in it with spiritual songs, in every week, and that we should not do in it the work of this world — the hosts — but that there be in it, in our gatherings of assembly, [works] for God; for it is His day; and in it [let us] work the works of God, in which the believers inherit the kingdom of God forever, and the life which shall not pass away from being saved.
44.3: And the works of this world — forever in them there is revealed the life forever; you are the life which passes away, and the world passes away.
44.4: God said: Work for the life of this world which passes away.
44.5: Two days, and on the day of the Sabbath, work for Me alone; for it is My day, and I will give you your joy instead of what you worked for Me — My kingdom forever, and My life forever, and My flower which does not fade; and I will bless you in your work in the six days which you work in it; and I will not put you into the in which you are.
44.6: that it may be for you on My day [a recompense] for what you worked for Me in it.
44.7: And when you have worked for Me your desires — the three lives, and the three portions, earthly and heavenly — and as you worked for Me [in] that which is, I separated you from my peoples and from my and from my joy forever; and I grieved you in the work of the flesh, which you made it; it is better than my work; and your food, which consumes you, the which shall be for you on My day, from the of which consumes you — or in the suffering of — I tried you in it, that you should give all your labor.
44.8: Or they steal your, or by they your.
44.9: Or destroy your seed, or slay that which was tried from your friend; and you shall be grieved, and you shall be sad on earth and in heaven; for I am He who enriches, and I make poor and I kill and I make alive.
44.10: Friend, this is the interpretation of the word of God concerning the day of the Sabbath: that it is the day in which it is not fitting that they should do in it a work which is not without work.
44.11: And the work is: His glory — of God — and His holiness, always; and the hearing of His holy books all the day long: this is the work of God which is fitting that they should do on the day of the Sabbath, which is the day of God; and by this work the believers live a good life, which is on earth and in heaven.
44.12: And concerning this it is fitting for the believers that they keep the commandment, and rejoice [in] the work of this world, and rest from him in this.
44.13: And many of the believers neglect in this from their works forever; they neglect God in this light; and their is greater than the of those who do the work of this world; for they do the work of this world, for they take their food in the life which passes away, which presses upon it, while they are in this world.

49.1: And concerning this, God commanded that we eat and drink and rejoice on the Sabbath day in full; and He commanded concerning the flesh — its name is the flesh of beasts, mingled — and He appointed a day for us, for the day; and it is confirmed by this word of God: He appointed for the flesh, food and drink; goes forth for the work of the Spirit on the Sabbath day; and He appointed upon it, in rest.
49.2: Behold, I have loved that which I have revealed to you; and take heed in your heart, and teach them the name of the Faith, and to others; for it is the foundation of the life which is eternal, and of the life of this world; and they rooted it in [the two] in earth and in heaven; and [there is] deliverance from judgment, and rest from the two works of toil, and riches from the hidden treasures in earth and in heaven.
49.3: For you know that which is written in [the book of] the Kings: that God appeared to Solomon, and said to him: "Ask of Me that which I shall give you."
49.4: And Solomon said to Him: "I have asked of You that You would give me a wise heart, that I may judge rightly in the midst of this great people."
49.5: The Scripture says: And God was pleased at this word; for he asked of Him a heavenly work, which abides, and he did not ask of Him an earthly work, which perishes.
49.6: And God said to him: "Because you have asked neither length of days, nor abundance of riches, nor the soul of your enemies, but you have asked wisdom — and it is the work which pleases Me — behold, I give you the wisdom which you have asked of Me, which I have given to none before you, nor after you."
49.7: "And I will add to you, above this, that which you have not asked of Me: length of days, and abundance of riches, and the soul of your enemies."
49.8: Behold, I have loved how Solomon, when he desired the work which abides alone, and did not seek the work which perishes, God gave him the abiding [thing] which he had asked, and added to him, above this, the perishing work which he had not asked; for He knew that which he desired.
49.9: And likewise He says in the Gospel: "Seek My kingdom and My righteousness, and I will add to you that which you desire of the work of this world, which is food and drink and clothing."
49.10: Likewise everyone who labors for the glory of God and His holiness, and hears His word on the Sabbath day in full, shall obtain in this kingdom of heaven: God shall give that [portion], and shall grant him good and rest from all that wearies, from the work of this world — food and drink and clothing — as He did to Solomon. And he who does not labor thus for the life of his soul, from the eternal kingdom, but inherits eternal judgment — God shall afflict him in this world, and shall weary him all the days of his life, and shall deprive him of the two rests together, in heaven and in earth; for God is mighty and able.
49.11: And he who labors for the day of the LORD, and shall be exalted with the LORD on the day of His resurrection in full — he also shall abide with the LORD on the day of the resurrection; he shall be exalted on the day of glory and honor, as it was done on earth on the Sabbath day. And he who does not labor for the glory of God and His holiness, and does not hear His word on the Sabbath day, shall go forth from the fathers of God and from His glory, as the Devil fell when he was withheld from glory and holiness on the Sabbath day: look, they are in it — they fell; and in it shall fall all who do not labor for the glory of God and His holiness, as they fell.
49.12: And behold, I have revealed to you in the book of Kasit, the spiritual writing, that for those who are weak in work, their portion is appointed upon them on the Sabbath day; and it is appointed for glory and for holiness at the times, twice on the Sabbath day: the morning, and two and a hundred and four, and the evening, within, upon the day which is read, all the day; for when they are steadfast [refraining] from the perishing work, it is fitting for them that they be joined to prayer at the times, within, upon the day which is read.
49.13: And on the two days also, the others — it is not fitting for them save for eating; it is not fitting for them save for eating, in the book — as I have shown you in the book of Helit of the host: they shall pray wherever they are, according to the measure of their strength and their knowledge, if they do not their work; and God listened to them.
49.14: I have loved: behold, I have shown you the glory of the Sabbath day; and in it is the life of the faithful, and their joy which is in earth and in heaven is upon them, and work is in it; and teach all whom you have found, [to them], the faithful; and behold, I have revealed to you the reason of the fast: one day, Wednesday and Friday, in the peace of God. Amen.

50.1: The second discourse, concerning the ordinances of the fast of the one day, Wednesday and Friday, which is the love of God: may He enlighten the eyes of your heart by the light of the Holy Spirit, the Comforter, that you may discern the mystery of the Godhead.

50.3: Wednesday and Friday, and always he observes

50.5: He is severed and cursed: if he is a priest,, and a stranger, and his curse [is] from God; and if he does not fast also the one day always — there is that which I have told you — that you may know the reason of this: when God brought forth the children of Israel
50.6: the land of Egypt, as they journeyed in their going forth, and afterwards He led them into the land of Canaan, which is the land of Jerusalem; and you are in it; and He gave them days over the nations, while they dwelt in it, being sent, and kings in it. And there were in their borders nations, Canaanites, while they spread into all the coasts of the shore of the sea, from Gaza and Ashkelon to the harbor of the sea of the Philistines, and Dan and the Canaanites.
